stemBlocks.value: The principal of Sunrise Secondary School wishes to estimate the number of students who favour a change in the lunch period. A systematic sample of 84 students is selected from the school population of 840 students. Of those selected, 61 favour the change. (a) State the population in this investigation. (b) State the sample. (c) Write the sample statistic as a fraction. (d) Explain why 61/84 is a sample statistic and not a population parameter. (e) Estimate the number of students in the school who favour the change.
Think first: Keep clear which group each number describes: the whole school or the 84 chosen from it.

solutionSteps.instruction: Identify the whole group being studied.

contentBlocks.value: The investigation is about the students of Sunrise Secondary School
Result: The 840 students of the school

solutionSteps.instruction: Form the sample proportion in favour.

contentBlocks.value: 61 of the 84 selected favour the change
It is calculated only from the 84 students surveyed, not from all 840
Result: A sample statistic, not a population parameter

solutionSteps.instruction: Scale the proportion up to the whole population.

strategyBlocks.value: Name the two groups, form the proportion in favour from the sample, explain what makes it a statistic, then scale that proportion up to the whole school.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) The population is all 840 students of Sunrise Secondary School.  (b) The sample is the 84 students selected.  (c) 61/84.  (d) Because it was calculated from the 84 students in the sample rather than from all 840 students in the school. A population parameter would require every member of the population to be surveyed; 61/84 is a measurement of the sample and is used only to estimate the corresponding population value.  (e) About 610 students.

whyThisWorks.value: A sample is used because measuring a whole population is often impractical, and a statistic computed from the sample stands in as an estimate of the unknown parameter. The estimate works by assuming the sample is representative, so the proportion in favour in the sample is taken to hold across the population. Since 84 is exactly one tenth of 840, multiplying 61 by 10 scales the count up in the same ratio.

examTip.value: In sampling questions, write down the population size and the sample size side by side before doing any arithmetic; the ratio between them drives every estimate.
